1. 제 3차 전도여행(에베소에서 헬라까지): 1. The Third Missionary Journey (from Ephesus to Greece)
<행19:21~22> 이 일이 다 된 후 바울이 마게도냐와 아가야로 다녀:
<Acts 19:21~22> After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome. So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
 - After wrapping up all his ministry in Ephesus, he plans to go to Macedonia and Achaia, then to Jerusalem, and then to Rome. And here Paul's ministry starts to get more and more organized: he sends an advance team ahead in the direction he plans to go, to get things ready in advance - to save Paul's time. And later you can also see him leaving a follow-up team behind.
<행19:23~26> 그 때쯤 되어 이 도로 인하여 적지 않은 소동이 있: <Acts 19:23~26> And the same time there arose no small stir about that way. For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith (a craftsman who works in silver), which made silver shrines (dwellings for the goddess made of silver) for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
아데미 – 풍요와 다산의 우상. 아르테미스, 다이아나, 앗수르의: Diana - the idol of abundance and fertility. Artemis, Diana, Assyria's
각 나라 왕들이 127개 기둥 하나씩 바쳐서 만든 신전, 어마 어마한 크: A temple built with each of its 127 pillars donated by the king of a nation - enormous in size
건축 기간만 120년, 길이 115m, 폭 55m, 높이 19m. 고대: Construction took 120 years; 115 m long, 55 m wide, 19 m high. The largest temple of the ancient world
신전 주위 300미터 이내 신성한 지역 : 범죄자들이 피신하면 못 잡아: Within 300 meters around the temple was sacred ground: criminals who fled there couldn't be arrested.
1,000 priestesses: called sacred prostitutes, they performed lewd acts.
Today only a single stone pillar like this remains.
그가 그 직공들과 이러한 영업하는 자들을 모아 이르되 여러분도 알거니와: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth. Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:
‘사람의 손으로 만든 것은 신이 아니다’이 한마디에 그 대단한 아데미 신: 'They be no gods, which are made with hands' - with that one sentence, that mighty Temple of Diana starts to wobble. Idol worship is the height of arrogance. I make it with my own hands and then call it a god. So who's higher? And idol worship is the height of foolishness. I've just made it, and then I bow down to it... That's the height of stupidity.
우상 만드는 사람들이 자신들의 수입이 줄어드는 것을 보고 극장에 모여서: The idol makers saw their income dropping, gathered in the theater, and all chaos broke loose.
이게 연극장인데 규모도 대단하지만 설계가 기가 막혀요. 원형으로 만들었고:
This is the theater, and not only is it huge, its design is amazing. It's built in a circle, and when the wind blows from the sea, you can hear even the sound of a coin dropping on the stage. Without any mic or amp...
 - So a big crowd gathered, and the people didn't even know why they had gathered, and for two hours they kept shouting, "Great is Diana! Great is Diana!" In the middle of all this, Paul sees so many people gathered that he thinks maybe he can preach to them, and tries to go into the theater, but his friends stop him. 'Teacher Paul, they want to kill you - do you know where you're going?' In the end the town clerk calms the crowd and barely gets them settled down.
 - After that event, Paul didn't say, 'I'll go and be martyred.' He realized it was time for him to leave and set off for Greece.
<행20:1~3a> 소요가 그치매 바울이 제자들을 불러 권한 후에 작별하:
<Acts 20:1~3a> And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto him the disciples, and embraced them, and departed for to go into ③ Macedonia. And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into ④ Greece, And there abode three months.
 - Hellas is Greece, of course. Corinth, Athens, the region of Achaia. While he stays three months in Greece, he writes Romans.
<행20:3~4> 거기 석 달을 있다가 배 타고 수리아로 가고자 할 그:
<Acts 20:3~4> And there abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia. And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
 - Just before Paul went back to Jerusalem, Titus was in Corinth preparing the offering, and Paul was also going around Macedonia and Greece collecting the offering. And he isn't just bringing money - representatives of several churches come along all together, so they can see for themselves that it's handled fairly.
 - Because Titus had gone to Corinth ahead of time and prepared well, these people could come along, and during the three months they stayed there, they could hold meetings steadily. It shows how organized Paul's missionary team was.
